- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing sustained downward trends.
- After sharp price spikes, model underreacts — forecasts remain high while true values decline more aggressively.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overestimates near recent highs and underestimates near recent lows.
- Forecasts often overshoot the true mean by 2–5% in the first 5–10 days, then gradually converge — suggesting a lag in adjusting to new information.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in the final 5–10 days of the forecast window, especially when true values show strong decline.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the middle of the horizon (days 15–25), while true values often dip below forecast mid-point.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 5–10 days, leading to underprediction of sharp drops or spikes.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” out volatility — underestimating sudden drops and overestimating gradual declines.
